outcome_branch: Early rejection at performance-leadership section6 step2: the entire request-header encode contribution is below1% of the representative complete micro-request workload in both CPU and instructions. No implementation candidate was created; remaining implementation/acceptance criteria do not apply.
hypothesis: Preencode client_id and other immutable request-header bytes on BrokerConn, patching correlation ID and frame length, to reduce per-request header encoding instructions while preserving classic/flexible wire bytes.
finding: The borrowed encoder already avoids temporary String allocation. For the named100-record Produce shape, default-client header encoding is only350 classic/396 flexible instructions, against complete frames of96252.595/115704.223 instructions. CPU shares are0.316230%/0.349153%; instruction shares0.363627%/0.342252%, below the visibility threshold. Eliminating all measured header work would still be a sub-percent effect for this shape; actual preencoding must retain copying and patching. A production cache was therefore not warranted by this named workload.

This is a read-only visibility probe, not a newly shipped benchmark cell or candidate A/B.

primary.metric: request-header instruction fraction of complete framed request, percent
primary.interpretation: Baseline cost visibility; both observed fractions below1%. No candidate A/B speedup exists.

instructions.unit: Callgrind Ir per inclusive encode_case invocation
instructions.collection_scope: Only inclusive header_cost_probe::encode_case calls (twenty warmups, one allocation census, N timed-loop calls); process/fixture/setup/output outside this function excluded. Divisor=N+21. No kernel instructions counted.
instructions.determinism: All five independently launched runs of each shape returned the same instruction count; degenerate bootstrap intervals report only these fixed binary/input observations.

cpu_visibility.unit: CPU ns per operation and matched-round header/full-frame fraction

classic_share.metric: header-only process CPU ns/op divided by full framed request process CPU ns/op
classic_share.interpretation: Visibility estimate, not a candidate speedup. The numerator also includes dispatch/clear/black-box overhead. Process startup/setup are amortized, not attributed as instructions.

flexible_share.metric: header-only process CPU ns/op divided by full framed request process CPU ns/op
flexible_share.interpretation: Visibility estimate, not a candidate speedup. The numerator also includes dispatch/clear/black-box overhead. Process startup/setup are amortized, not attributed as instructions.

Existing named micro-request case is body-only; it cannot alone measure a header cache. The supplemental probe includes actual headers and complete frames while leaving the original cell/input and ratcheted baselines unchanged.

No production candidate, no candidate SHA, no candidate A/B comparison, no accepted optimization and no candidate guardrail delta. The early outcome branch applies; five baseline-shape rounds are not five candidate acceptance pairs.

Default13-byte client id, Produce classicv8/flexiblev9,100records,16-byte keys,100-byte random values,zero record headers and retained16KiB buffer only. Tiny metadata/auth bodies, long or invalid client IDs, other API versions and unknown incoming tags are not benchmarked; their unchanged code is covered only by existing tests where applicable.

Header instruction numerator includes correlation-ID work and dispatch/clear/black-box overhead; actual preencoding still must copy bytes and patch mutable fields. This is a visibility estimate, not a universal optimization speedup bound.

CPU/rusage includes process setup and warmup amortized across large loops; wall values are kept separately. Managed shared host has no frequency pinning or isolation of host-wide memory/cache effects.

Callgrind instructions are deterministic for this fixed binary/input and do not measure kernel/network/TLS/DNS cost. Degenerate confidence intervals reflect repeated identical counts, not coverage of unmeasured workloads.
